🔻 Imam Khamenei turned Islamic unity into practical movement: Lebanese scholar

📌 TEHRAN, Iran — Lebanese scholar Sayyed Ali Fadlallah, a former Friday prayer leader of Beirut, says that the martyred Leader of the Islamic Revolution, Ayatollah Seyyed Ali Khamenei, went beyond theoretical discussions of Islamic unity and turned it into a practical program for the Muslim community.

Speaking to IRNA on the sidelines of the 40th International Islamic Unity Conference in Iran, held under the supervision of the World Forum for Proximity of Islamic Schools of Thought, Fadlallah praised the role of martyred Imam Khamenei in strengthening Islamic unity.
​
Fadlallah said the late Leader’s religious rulings and positions on Muslim history and relations, particularly between Sunni and Shiite Muslims, represented a rare intellectual reference on the issue of unity.
​
He said unity was not presented as a temporary slogan but as a way of life for Muslims, based on common foundations including the Quran and the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH), and aimed at promoting coexistence and solidarity among Muslims.
​
On the role of the Islamic Republic in promoting unity, Fadlallah said Iran had presented a distinctive model by moving beyond conferences and slogans and demonstrating its commitment to unity through the sacrifices of its leaders and martyrs in support of Palestine and human dignity.
​
He said Imam Khamenei had consistently sought to present an Islamic, independent, sovereign, and powerful model that could serve as a source of support for oppressed and freedom-seeking people around the world.
​
Fadlallah identified three main foundations of the late leader’s approach to Islamic unity: the Quran, the Ahl al-Bayt and the Karbala school, and the establishment of an Islamic, independent and powerful model.
​
Regarding the Quran, he said Imam Khamenei encouraged Muslims and humanity as a whole to reflect on its teachings, contributing to a broader movement in the Islamic world focused on a substantive and interpretive understanding of Islam rather than merely its outward forms.
​
On the issue of Palestine, Fadlallah said Imam Khamenei’s approach emphasized connecting different generations with the Palestinian cause.

“Russia Will Not Hit NATO Or Any Of the Baltic States”


European officials are certain there is no evidence that Russia is preparing for a conventional military attack against NATO or any of the Baltic states. 

They are “pushing back” on media reports that preventing an attack on NATO was the focus of CIA Director John Ratcliffe’s visit to Moscow this week.

“Topics on the visit would likely have included ending the war against Ukraine, reaffirming the strength of NATO’s Article 5 commitment in the face of a potential attack, and the Iran war, according to people familiar with the matter, who asked not to be identified because of the sensitivity of the issue,” Reuters writes.

“None of the officials had been briefed by the U.S. on the details of Ratcliffe’s meeting, and their assessments were based on their own intelligence and their understanding of how the United States typically operates.”

One Bloomberg source said the visit to Moscow was also likely intended to prevent an excessive Russian response to U.S. economic measures against Iran that could affect Russia, and to persuade Moscow to stop supporting Tehran.

Western intelligence and government officials have warned in recent months that Russian security services are exploring options for sabotage against infrastructure and false-flag operations in the Baltic states and Poland.

At the same time, the sources said the latest intelligence did not indicate any changes in Russia’s conventional military posture.

Western intelligence services routinely maintain communication channels with their Russian counterparts, officials said. However, people familiar with the trip suggested that it was notable that Ratcliffe appeared to want his Moscow visit to become public.

📄 Iran, Iraq ramp up work to launch joint free zone

📌 Ilam, IRNA – Iranian and Iraqi officials have emphasized accelerating the implementation of legal mechanisms and launching the joint free zone.

On Saturday, Iranian Ambassador to Baghdad, Mohammad-Kazem Ale-Sadegh, and Mehdi Rayati, the CEO of the Mehran Free Zone, held a joint meeting with Munther Abdul-Amir Assad, the Director General of Iraq’s General Authority for Free Zones, to review the latest measures, as well as the technical, legal, and administrative requirements for implementing the strategic project, including the projected timeline.
​
The two sides emphasized the commitment of Iranian and Iraqi officials to enhance economic ties. They highlighted the need for improved coordination among executive bodies, the finalization of the plan, and the establishment of conditions to attract private-sector investment.
​
During the meeting, Rayati said that launching the joint commercial and industrial crossing would create a unique opportunity to connect production chains between Iran and Iraq, establish export-oriented joint industries, and lower trade and goods transit costs.
​
For his part, Abdul-Amir Assad welcomed expanded cooperation with Iran, adding that the Iraqi side is ready to finalize coordination with the relevant authorities in Baghdad and Wasit Governorate to establish essential infrastructure at the Zurbatiyah border point.
